inputs.text: [happily] Listen: amphibians now live on land. [curious] But they're still missing something.
[calm] They always have to go back near the water to lay their eggs, [softly] or the eggs dry out. [serious] So life comes up with a fix.
[excited][amazed] An egg with a hard shell, [gasps] that keeps the water inside! [happily] And that's how the very first true reptiles appear.
[amazed] So they can lay their eggs anywhere?
[playful] Exactly! Even far from water, right in the desert. [calm] This time is called the Permian.
[curious] And are the continents like today?
[serious][calm] Not at all! All the continents are stuck together in one giant block: Pangea. [softly] The name means "all the Earth," in Greek.
[amazed] All around it, one single enormous ocean. [pauses] And in the middle of the block, so far from the sea that the climate gets very, very dry: a giant desert.
[gasps] Were there dinosaurs in that desert?

[chuckles][softly] Not yet! [playful] There is an animal with a big sail on its back, Dimetrodon, [serious] but it's not a dinosaur: it's a distant cousin of the mammals. [calm] Dinosaurs show up forty million years later.
[nervous] What happens next in that desert?
[serious][softly] The climate keeps getting drier, and harder. [pauses] And far beneath our feet, something is brewing...
